title: Etale horizontal compact-support exchange is the composition mate
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. All schemes below are Noetherian, meaning they admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. In a Cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product]
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X'&\xrightarrow{u'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow u&Y,\end{array}$$
assume that $f,f',u,u'$ are separated finite-type morphisms, $u,u'$ are etale, and give these morphisms and their equal composites $fu'=uf'$ compactifications [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale sites and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Put $F_a=Ra_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and $S_a=D(a_{\Sigma!})$ for $a=u,u'$, with the sum/evaluation adjunction $S_a\dashv a^*$ and counit $\epsilon_a$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Let $d_a:F_a\xrightarrow{\sim}S_a$ be the canonical proper-support comparison of [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], followed by its identification of proper-support sections with the sum extension. Use the specified proper/open composition maps and compact-support exchange $C_{f,u}:u^*F_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f'}u'^*$ of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Define
$$\delta=(d_uF_{f'})\circ\alpha_{u,f'}^{-1}\circ\alpha_{f,u'}\circ F_f(d_{u'}^{-1}):F_fS_{u'}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_uF_{f'}.$$
For every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the following equality holds:
$$F_f(\epsilon_{u',M})\circ\delta_{u'^*M}^{-1}=\epsilon_{u,F_fM}\circ S_u(C_{f,u,M}^{-1}):S_uF_{f'}u'^*M\longrightarrow F_fM.$$
Equivalently, the left side has adjunct $C_{f,u,M}^{-1}$ under $S_u\dashv u^*$. This equality uses the specified compactification exchange, not an arbitrary natural isomorphism with the same endpoints.

proof.text: First prove that every comparison N.comparison(e,c) is the explicit canonicalEtaleCompactSupportComparison. The inclusion of open extension into direct image is sectionwise injective by the open-extension proper-support range theorem; direct-image precomposition and its composition isomorphism preserve this monomorphism. Cancel it in the sheaf_normalization equations for N and the canonical graph core. Precomposition with homotopy localization is faithful, so the two derived_normalization equations identify the inverse comparison natural transformations, and hence the isomorphisms. This is the proved private normalization_comparison_eq_canonical lemma.

Choose the given compactification c=(j,p) of f and its pullback c′=(j′,p′). Put J=Dj!, J′=Dj′!, P=Rp*, Q=Rp′*, B=S_b, R=b*, L=S_v and S=v*, where b is the pulled-back etale map on the ambient schemes. The specified proper exchange ex:P S -> R Q is invertible by torsion-ring proper base change. The explicit inverse-image square agrees after transporting total-derived upper star through its exact-derived comparison. Transport invertibility across these isomorphic left adjoints: the conjugate comparisons on right adjoints are automatically isomorphisms. This proves invertibility of exactDerivedBaseChangeMap without requiring an equality between the two chosen adjunction structures.

For the proper square put tau equal to its exact inverse-image comparison and sumEx equal to its inverse mate under the actual localized sum/evaluation adjunctions. The iterated-mates identity identifies conjugate(sumEx) under the two composite adjunctions with ex. Conjugacy reflects isomorphisms, so sumEx is invertible. Conjugacy also preserves its inverse; iterating mates in the other order identifies the right-adjoint mate of inverse sumEx with the inverse mate of inverse ex. This is the proved generic rotated_inverse_mate calculation. Apply the canonical graph tower identity to c and v′*M, then replace its canonical comparisons with N using step 1. It writes delta inverse as L(t′ inverse), Gamma, P(a), and t, where Gamma is now the inverse mate of inverse ex.

For the open square, write its sheaf base-change map as the inverse mate of squareUpperStarIso under the two open-extension adjunctions. The iterated-mates/conjugacy identity proves this directly from the definition of open base change. Its unit equation descends under mapDerivedCategoryAdjunction_mate. Apply the iterated-mates identity again, now with the actual localized etale adjunctions on the horizontal arrows. Thus a is the inverse mate of the exact-derived open base-change isomorphism beta. The mate counit equation gives a at v′*M followed by J(epsilon_v′,M) = B(beta.hom_M) followed by epsilon_b at J(M).

The unit equation of the mate defining Gamma gives adj_L(Gamma_H) followed by ex_(B H) = Q(eta_b,H). Naturality of ex, beta.hom followed by beta.inv = identity, and the right triangle for b show that adj_L(Gamma_H followed by P(B(beta.hom) followed by epsilon_b)) followed by ex_(J M) followed by Q(beta.inv) is identity. This is proved as the generic private interchange_mate lemma, without assuming that the etale adjunction unit is invertible. Naturality of t moves the v′ counit through the last factor of the tower formula; step 4 then identifies the parent left-hand side with this generic composite transported by t and t′.

Use unboundedEtaleCompactSupport_baseChange and exchange_normalization to write the specified compact-support exchange C on M as S(t inverse) followed by ex_(J M), Q(beta.inv), and t′_(v′*M). Transport the identity in step 5 through t,t′ using adjunction naturality. Cancellation of C.hom identifies the adjunct of the parent left-hand side with C.inv. Applying the inverse adjunction hom equivalence gives exactly the requested sum-extension/counit expression.

lean.statement: theorem etaleHorizontalSupportMate (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] {X X' Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian X'] [IsNoetherian Y] [IsNoetherian Y'] {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {v : Y' ⟶ Y} {v' : X' ⟶ X} [IsSeparated f] [IsSeparated f'] [IsSeparated v] [IsSeparated v'] [Etale v] [Etale v'] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f'] [LocallyOfFiniteType v] [LocallyOfFiniteType v'] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiCompact f'] [QuasiCompact v] [QuasiCompact v'] [HasCompactification f] [HasCompactification f'] [HasCompactification v] [HasCompactification v'] [HasCompactification (v' ≫ f)] [HasCompactification (f' ≫ v)] [QuasiCompact (v' ≫ f)] [QuasiCompact (f' ≫ v)] (sq : IsPullback v' f' f v) (N : EtaleCompactSupportNormalization A) : ∀ (M : DerivedCategoryModule A X), (etaleHorizontalSupportMateDelta A sq N).inv.app ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) v').mapDerivedCategory.obj M) ≫ (rightDerivedLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).map ((derivedEtaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) v' inferInstance).counit.app M) = (etaleLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) v inferInstance).mapDerivedCategory.map ((etaleHorizontalSupportBaseChangeIso A sq).inv.app M) ≫ (derivedEtaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) v inferInstance).counit.app ((rightDerivedLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).obj M)
lean.note: The theorem renders the node’s constant-etale-module derived categories as DerivedCategoryModule, F_a as rightDerivedLowerShriek, S_a as the etale lower-shriek (sum-extension) functor, d_a through the explicit normalization comparison, and C_{f,u} as the canonical unbounded compact-support base-change isomorphism. The three preceding declarations are the canonical comparison, composition mate, and inverse base-change interface used by the theorem. The normalized d_a is etaleCanonicalCompactSupportComparison, built from N : EtaleCompactSupportNormalization A, the landed declaration of lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization (Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleCompactSupportNormalization). The recorded declaration of lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact is an existence theorem with no usable comparison data. N fixes the same graph-normalized proper-support-to-sum comparison: sheaf_normalization pins its sheaf map into the direct image, which is mono, and derived_normalization pins its derived descent, so every N gives the same d_a. This is the convention of lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality and lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility. The counits epsilon_a are those of AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.derivedEtaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction, the termwise sum/evaluation adjunction of the published build that the live lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality statement also uses. etaleHorizontalSupportBaseChangeIso is C_{f,u} itself; the statement uses its inv, C_{f,u}^{-1}.
